summary: Model output arriving a token at a time, in a container that does not move. Deliberately not a live region.
useWhen: rendering a response that streams in rather than arriving whole
the reader should be able to start reading before generation finishes

useInstead.why: nothing about this component helps once there is nothing left to arrive

useInstead.when: you are showing progress through steps rather than producing text

a11y.role: region when `label` is set, none otherwise
guarantees: `aria-live="off"`, deliberately — a polite live region re-announces the whole answer on every token, which makes a streaming response unusable with a screen reader
`aria-busy` while streaming, so assistive tech knows the region is unsettled
the text stays ordinary readable content throughout, so a screen-reader user can read ahead exactly as a sighted user does
the cursor is `aria-hidden`, is a styled box rather than a text character, and stops blinking under `prefers-reduced-motion` (WCAG 2.3.1)
requires: announcing completion yourself, with your own `role="status"`, if the surface wants it — a chat with ten turns on screen does not want ten announcements
`label` when the region needs a name of its own

antiPatterns.why: every token queues an announcement; the user hears the answer stuttered dozens of times and cannot get ahead of it

antiPatterns.dont: letting the container grow token by token with no reserved height
antiPatterns.why: the content below climbs the screen while someone is reading it, which is worse under magnification than the wait
some screen readers read it aloud even inside an aria-hidden span
